_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: One key added, springdoc.swagger-ui.version=@swagger-ui.version@, Maven-filtered from the new swagger-ui.version property in backend/pom.xml, which pins the org.webjars:swagger-ui webjar to 5.34.1 (DOMPurify 3.4.17) ahead of the 5.32.14 springdoc manages; the nightly OWASP scan failed on five DOMPurify advisories against the older bundle (#806). The key only names the versioned webjar directory springdoc serves /swagger-ui/** from, so the UI resolves when it is switched on. Section 1's springdoc claim holds: springdoc.api-docs.enabled and springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled still default to false, the PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS list is untouched, and repackage and process-aot still exclude both org.springdoc and the swagger-ui webjar (check:repackage-excludes agrees on the same 9 artifacts), so the sidecar serves nothing new and carries no new code. No other key changed. Verdict unchanged.

#815. FolderResponse, the body of GET /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/folders, gains a nullable parentRef: the folderRef of another folder in the same response, or null. It carries nothing the response did not hold: every value is a folderRef already in that list, and the folder names were in it already as folderRef and displayName. The compact constructor drops a blank parentRef or one equal to the folder's own ref; a four-argument constructor keeps the old shape with parentRef null. No endpoint, request body, validation, authentication or error path changed, and no other DTO in the package moved; the OpenAPI snapshot gains the one field. Verdict unchanged.

One key added, springdoc.swagger-ui.version=@swagger-ui.version@, Maven-filtered from the swagger-ui webjar pin in backend/pom.xml (5.34.1, DOMPurify 3.4.17, for the five DOMPurify advisories that failed the nightly scan, #806). It only names the webjar directory springdoc serves Swagger UI from in dev; this audit makes no claim about springdoc, and no mail.client.*, spring.mail.*, IMAP, SMTP, timeout, sync or connection key moved. Verdict unchanged.

#812, recorded in the audit as 1.84 (§5) and waiting for its independent pass. BoundedImapProtocol.parseBounded reads a FETCH that Angus rejected once more with each empty list in its structure written NIL (EmptyListsAsNil, new), for the ("inline" ()) disposition Seznam writes. Only after the rejection, at most 1 MiB, and only a () inside a BODYSTRUCTURE or BODY value after a string or an atom; what it hands back goes through the same DepthBoundedFetchResponse and type check, so no bound moves, and the copy it makes is at most 1.5 MiB. A FETCH it does not rescue is now logged with Angus's reason, cut to 200 characters, before the skip it always had. Verdict unchanged.

Folder display order. FolderDisplayOrder (new) sorts the list MailFacade.getFolders returns to GET /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/folders: INBOX, its USER subfolders (unless a system folder also lives under INBOX, the Courier namespace layout), the other system roles in a fixed order, then USER folders by path in the request's collation. It is an in-memory sort of the FolderResponse list ImapFolderService already produced: no IMAP command, no folder opened, no bound moved, and nothing held beyond a copy of the list. The cached list and every internal caller of ImapFolderService.getFolders (the sync's folder listing, role resolution, the move target check) keep the server's order, and folders sharing a role keep their relative order in the sorted list too, so the folder a role resolves to does not move. Verdict unchanged.

#815, folder hierarchy. ImapFolderService.listFolders gives each FolderResponse a parentRef: the nearest ancestor, by Folder.getSeparator(), that is in the same listing (an ancestor spelled Inbox finds INBOX), else null. The delimiter is the one Angus holds from the LIST response for every listed folder, so no IMAP command is added and no folder is opened; the walk cuts the folder's own name at each delimiter and looks the prefix up in a map of the listed names, so it is bounded by the name's length and holds nothing beyond the listing. A MessagingException from getSeparator is logged at TRACE and leaves the folder top-level instead of failing the listing. FolderDisplayOrder now orders from parentRef rather than from the delimiter read out of folderRef: roots in the fixed role order, each followed by its subfolders, walked with its own stack so a hierarchy as deep as the server makes it cannot overflow the request thread (FolderDisplayOrderTest places 100,000 levels; the recursive form overflows on it, run and seen). The parentRef it returns is the display one: a system folder is top-level, and on the Courier namespace layout INBOX's children are. Still an in-memory reorder of the list ImapFolderService produced, which the cache and the internal callers keep in the server's order and with the server's parentRef; folders sharing a role keep their relative order. Verdict unchanged.

Change under this path, read rather than waved through as a timing tweak. StartupTimingService swapped its reference clock: the anchor for processStartedAt and for every phase's startedAfterProcessMs moved from an Instant.now() taken in the class's own static initialiser to ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getStartTime(), with a wall-clock constant recording how much boot had already passed when the class loaded. Section 1 is untouched by it: the diff does not enter StorageContextInitializer, reads or writes no crypto.bin, touches neither the VOXSEC1 format, the DPAPI USER-scope call, the buffer zeroing, the atomic private-permissioned write, nor the constant-time crypto.fingerprint comparison, and adds no path by which any of them could be reached earlier or skipped. The class holds no secret and opens no file. Section 2 holds: CryptoService is not in the diff, and the one place where boot timing and that section intersect - the self-test "warmed off the boot path" claim - is about when the self-test runs, which this change does not move; it only changes what a later dump reports about the time that had already elapsed. The new dependency is java.management, read-only and already in the sidecar's --add-modules list; it is an MXBean read, not a JNI or FFM call, so the "pure Java FFM (no JNI)" hygiene claim of section 1 is about a path this does not join. Section 3 residuals are unaffected - nothing about mail.db plaintext at rest or the same-user-malware exclusion turns on a clock source. The one observable effect outside the boundary is that startup-timings.json in the diagnostic dump now reports a start roughly four seconds earlier and correspondingly larger phase offsets: the same data category as before, no new field and no new value class, and the dump's privacy check is RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 7, which is flagged for a re-take on this candidate for exactly this reason.

Recorded in the audit itself as v1.2: the PBKDF2 iteration count moves from CryptoProperties (mail.crypto.pbkdf2-iterations, @Min 1000, default 600000) to a private constant PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 600_000 in CryptoService, and CryptoProperties.java joins Code paths with this entry, so a format value cannot come back as a property unseen. The bean constructor is now @Autowired and passes the constant to a package-private constructor that takes the count, which CryptoServiceTest uses with 1000; getOrDeriveKey reads the field where it read the property. Section 2 holds with the same values: AES/GCM, 12-byte IV, 128-bit tag, PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 at 600,000 over global salt || accountId to 256 bits, accountId as AAD, the self-test, the LRU and the shutdown hygiene are byte-identical, and a ciphertext pinned in CryptoServiceTest from the production constructor decrypts (changing the constant to 700_000 fails it, run and seen). Section 1 is untouched: core/init and core/security/secret did not change. Verdict stays PASS.

#816. DatabaseBackupService.previousAppVersion skips the file named after the current version (backup-pre-v<appVersion>) before taking the newest backup by modification time; createPreMigrationBackup runs before Flyway and wrote that file first, so the app_started audit record named the running version instead of the one updated from. The method only reads directory entries and returns a version string for the audit log. The backup itself is unchanged: VACUUM INTO through a bound parameter, the idempotent per-version name, the partial-file cleanup on failure, the retention prune and the backup's plaintext status as a copy of mail.db (AR-1 in section 3) are all as audited. No key material, crypto.bin path or file permission is touched. Verdict unchanged.

The forwarder's Shift branch of the preventDefault predicate grows from /^[rg]$/i to /^[rgi]$/i, so Ctrl+Shift+I (the app's new go-to-Inbox shortcut in globalShortcuts.ts) is cancelled in the frame as Ctrl+Shift+R and Ctrl+Shift+G are; the rest of the script is byte-identical, and the comment above it names the new key. MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT_SHA256 was recomputed independently (SHA-256 of the string literal, base64: yOywlma3ATltbXiySWrZF0tBX1RtZ0aZRF07BflnLk0=) and matches the constant and mailFrame.test.ts. Section 1 holds: the frame is still sandbox=allow-scripts without allow-same-origin, the CSP still admits exactly that one hash-pinned script, the forwarder still relays only isTrusted keystrokes and anchor clicks and posts the same fields; cancelling one more chord adds no capability and no data to what it sends. The styles, the sanitizer and the other Code paths are untouched. Verdict unchanged.

The only change under message-detail is the remote-image banner in MessageContent.svelte, for testers who could not tell what it was for: its text moves from a muted span to a paragraph that says why the images are held back (the message holds images from the internet that were not loaded, and loading them can tell the sender it was opened), and the i18n strings behind it, the region name and both announcements say 'images from the internet' instead of 'remote images'; the second button is now named 'Always load images from this sender'. The banner is still shown only while renderAsHtml, the count is non-zero and loadRemoteImages is false; the two buttons call the same revealRemoteImages and trustSender, which still send the same allow-list PUT; loadRemoteImages is still seeded per stableId from remoteImagesAllowedForSender; the iframe's sandbox, srcdoc, CSP and the mailFrame message handling are byte-identical. Section 1's tracking-pixel claim holds: no path loads a remote image without one of the two presses. The 2026-07-08 finding record still quotes the button's old English label, which is that date's record and not a claim about the current text. Verdict unchanged.

A javadoc in SecurityConfig.pkceAuthorizationRequestResolver now names client_secret_basic, Spring's default for the google registration, where it said client_secret_post (OAUTH_AUDIT.md section 4 note). Comment only: the filter chain, PKCE, CORS and the handlers are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

Two section 4 notes acted on, recorded in the audit itself as v1.6. ExternalProviderLoginService: findOrCreateExternalAccount still looks up (oauth2_provider, external_id) first, then the address, but the address now takes only a row with no oauth2_provider and no external_id (the password upgrade the fallback was written for); a row another identity owns makes the sign-in throw AccountAlreadyExistsException (409, error.account.alreadyExists) before any write, so the row, its binding and its token stay as they are, inside the same transaction that rolls back. markRequiresReauthIfExists takes (providerName, externalId, reason) and finds the account by findByOauth2ProviderAndExternalId instead of findByEmail, and the audit line carries the reason. Under feature/auth only OAuth2LoginService changes: its two callers pass providerName, externalId (validated non-blank by the guard before them) and missing_refresh_token or missing_scope. The four guards, their order, the flag's one clearing path, PKCE, the redirect handling, the session end at /success and the token storage are untouched. What moves narrows what a sign-in may touch: an account another identity owns can no longer be re-bound or flagged by it. Verdict stays PASS.

auth-finished.html and auth-failed.html, the pages the system browser shows after a sign-in, change for WCAG 2.2 only: the English half of each is marked lang="en" (3.1.2), the reason line on the failure page is #4b5563 instead of #6b7280 on #f3f4f6 (4.39:1 to 1.4.3's 4.5:1), and its Czech text uses the en dash. Markup and CSS only: the inline script that writes ?reason= with textContent, the redirect targets and the public-endpoint list are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

ExternalProviderLoginService takes the provider template from the OAuth registration the sign-in went through (AccountProviderService.resolveOAuthProvider, a lookup by mail_providers.oauth2_registration_id) instead of from the domain of the address the provider returned, so a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace account at an organization's own domain gets an account instead of ProviderNotFoundException. The template only fills a new row's server settings: the lookup order of findOrCreateExternalAccount, the refusal of an address another identity owns, the credential write, the after-commit invalidation and the reauth clear are unchanged, and a missing template still throws before any write. What a sign-in can reach narrows rather than widens: an address at another provider's domain no longer gives a new row that provider's servers, so a token is only ever presented to the servers of the provider that issued it. Under feature/auth nothing changes. Verdict unchanged.

The only change under frontend/src-tauri/src is redact.rs, the Save logs ZIP's redactor, which is the API surface audit's subject (A4, its 1.21): the mark walk that copied Java's \b is gone, so a token right after a non-spacing mark is replaced, and the comments now describe the Java side's hand scan. No updater command, capability, endpoint, version pin, signature check or install step is touched, and redact.rs is not on the update path: it runs only when the user saves the logs. Verdict unchanged.

#817, the v0.2.0-beta.1 cut. The one change in tauri.conf.json is the top-level version, 0.1.0 to 0.2.0-beta.1, written by bump:version. plugins.updater (endpoints, pubkey) and bundle (the NSIS template, installMode) are untouched. No claim of the audit rests on the value: the version pin compares the manifest with the version the prompt named, the build gate compares the tag with this field, and a prerelease orders after 0.1.0 and before 0.2.0 under semver, which is the order the beta channel and the later promotion need. Verdict unchanged.
